structural-causal.name: alignment2036
structural-causal.basis: Phosphate and potash replenish crop nutrients that support agricultural output.

structural-causal.name: bottleneckControl
structural-causal.basis: Mosaic controls meaningful nutrient production assets, but sulfur/input economics can become the binding constraint.

structural-causal.name: scenarioRobustness
structural-causal.basis: Food production need is durable while fertilizer affordability, crop economics and input costs remain cyclical.

structural-causal.name: substitutionResilience
structural-causal.basis: Farmers can optimize rates and nutrient sources, but phosphorus and potassium requirements cannot be eliminated indefinitely without yield/soil tradeoffs.

discovery-weak-signals.name: crop-nutrient essentiality versus input-cost pressure
discovery-weak-signals.basis: The business supplies essential potash/phosphate inputs, but sulfur-cost inflation was severe enough to curtail SSP production in Brazil.

adversarial-red-team.name: inputCostExposure
adversarial-red-team.basis: Sulfur inflation was severe enough to extend production curtailments.

adversarial-red-team.name: commodityCyclicality
adversarial-red-team.basis: Nutrient need persists, but realized margins depend on fertilizer prices, crop economics, supply response and feedstock costs.

adversarial-red-team.name: confidenceInflation
adversarial-red-team.basis: Product essentiality and a dividend should not be extrapolated into durable margin resilience.

expectations-execution.name: operational discipline
expectations-execution.basis: Curtailment can protect economics but also signals real cost pressure and lost production opportunity.

thesisQuality.basis: Essential phosphate/potash demand and global customer reach support durable utility, while commodity/input economics limit moat quality.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q2 revenue was $2.8B and adjusted EBITDA $407M, but GAAP operating loss was $36M and net loss $273M amid elevated sulfur costs.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Current market capitalization is about $7.5B after a material one-year share-price decline, but depressed earnings make simple P/E support weak; valuation is balanced rather than clearly cheap.

catalystScore.basis: Lower 2026 capex and portfolio rationalization can improve cash economics, but timing of sulfur normalization and phosphate recovery is uncertain.

governancePower.basis: Proxy documents stock-ownership requirements and management has taken explicit asset/capex actions tied to returns; CEO ownership remained below stated guideline at year-end 2025, tempering alignment.

alignment2036.basis: Phosphate and potash are essential agricultural nutrients serving food-system productivity across more than 40 countries.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Potash, phosphates, Brazilian distribution and biosciences create several agricultural demand channels, but they remain correlated to crop economics.

bottleneckControl.basis: Mosaic controls substantial nutrient production assets, but Q2 sulfur pricing and Brazilian idling show critical feedstock economics can shift the bottleneck away from owned capacity.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Food nutrient demand is durable, yet profitability remains exposed to fertilizer prices, crop economics and sulfur/input cycles.

substitutionResilience.basis: Phosphorus and potassium are agronomically necessary nutrients, though application intensity and product sourcing can change.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Global production footprint provides some diversification, but sulfur exposure was severe enough to idle Brazilian operations and Q3 sulfur contracts settled at $705/long ton.

pricingPower.basis: Essentiality supports demand but Q2 losses and sulfur-driven curtailments show limited ability to consistently pass input shocks through at attractive margins.

riskEvidence.basis: Commodity cyclicality, sulfur/feedstock inflation and asset-utilization pressure are material; Q2 GAAP loss and Brazilian idling provide direct evidence.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Recent SEC earnings evidence, proxy governance evidence, issuer operating updates and independent current market data cover all components, while detailed long-run unit economics and current fertilizer spot economics remain incomplete.

scoreRecord.thesis: Mosaic owns strategically relevant fertilizer capacity tied to durable food-system needs, but current underwriting is constrained by commodity cyclicality and unusually high sulfur/input costs.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Persistent sulfur and fertilizer-cycle pressure can keep phosphate assets underutilized and suppress cash returns despite durable nutrient demand.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Evidence of sulfur-cost normalization, improved phosphate margins/utilization, or further portfolio/capex discipline in the next reported quarter.

scoreBreakdown.note: earthScore is the Methodology 1.0 weighted component score; risk and confidence are separately recorded gate inputs and are not silently transformed into component values.
